ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Sir John Franklin

code.originalText: Pre-departure review two weeks before sailing: blood pressure, medicines and supplies, mental health, vaccinations, the medical kit and the evacuation plan

text.paragraph: Pre-departure review two weeks before sailing. [S]

Sir John sails in two weeks. His home readings this week average 126/78 on amlodipine 5 mg, with no side effects. He has lost 3.9 kg since intake by his own plan and counts his weight goal as met. He is sleeping well and is busy and cheerful; he knows the polar winters will be long and dark and has planned a routine of work, lessons and exercise for the officers and men. He has his clothing, a home blood pressure monitor with a spare cuff, and copies of his medical plan for the ship's surgeons. He has had every planned vaccine except the second zoster dose, due today. [S]

tr.td: No chest pain, palpitations or ankle swelling
Trouble hearing in noisy rooms, unchanged
Mood good; no worry he cannot manage

Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) 250 mg oral tablet once daily for the whole expedition, stored sealed and away from heat and light, in addition to food sources
One tablet by mouth daily from departure
Oseltamivir 75 mg oral capsule twice daily for five days
One capsule by mouth twice a day for five days

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-05-05; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 126/76, pulse 68; weight 86.9 kg, BMI 30.1; waist 101 cm

Hands, feet and face intact; no old cold injury

S — Synthetic laboratory finding at intake.

list.item:
Essential hypertension on amlodipine (I10). Controlled at 126/78 at home on amlodipine 5 mg; kidney function and potassium normal as a baseline for the years away. [S]
Amlodipine 5 mg daily: a three-year supply in blister packs, split between the two ships.
Weekly home readings on board; written instructions for the ship's surgeons to raise the dose to 10 mg if readings stay above 135/85 for a month, and to halve or stop it for dizziness, fainting or readings below 110 systolic during illness or heavy work.

Vitamin D insufficiency (E55.9). Now sufficient at 34 ng/mL. [S]
Continue vitamin D3 daily through the expedition.

Expedition preparation (Z71.84). Fit for the command. Vitamin C 250 mg daily is started now and stored sealed, cool and dark, because the vitamin C in stored juice and food loses strength over months; signs of scurvy (tiredness, sore gums, easy bruising, poor wound healing) to be reported to the surgeons. Mental health baseline normal. [S]
Vitamin C 250 mg daily from today.
Medical kit reviewed with the expedition's medical officer by letter: supplies for wounds, burns, frostbite, dental emergencies, infection and pain.
Evacuation plan: no evacuation possible for months at a time; serious illness is managed on board under his written wishes.
Second zoster dose today.
Review of medicines, blood pressure and weight on his return.
